exercise.name: Lever Assisted Chin-up

reference.title: Lever Assisted Chin-up
reference.listing: Video (movement reference only; the page could not be fetched from the authoring environment (gymvisual.com refused the request), so the data sheet was not read and the movement follows the exercise name and standard coaching)

equipment: Assisted pull-up machine (counterweighted lever knee pad, overhead handles)

breathing.pattern: Breathe out as you pull up, breathe in as you lower.
breathing.cadence: About 1.3 s up, short pause, about 2 s down

prescription.effort: Stop 1-3 reps short of failure (RIR 1-3, clinical opinion)
prescription.load: Assistance is user-chosen: more counterweight means a lighter pull.
prescription.progression: Add reps, then reduce the counterweight

cues.text: Take the bar with an underhand (palms toward you) grip about shoulder width and kneel on the pad; hang with the arms nearly straight.
Breathe out and pull the chest toward the bar, elbows travelling down in front of the body.
Pause with the chin over the bar and the shoulders down.
Breathe in and lower under control on the counterweighted pad.
Reach a full hang with the arms nearly straight.

mistakes.fix: Keep the knees on the pad and pull with the arms.
Lower to nearly straight arms each rep.
Set the shoulder blades down before each pull.
Pull the chest toward the handles; keep the neck long.

kinematics.norm: From nearly straight at the bottom to well bent with the chin over the handles (clinical opinion)
Supinated: underhand, about shoulder width (clinical opinion)
The body rises nearly straight up; the knees ride the counterweighted pad (clinical opinion)
The counterweight under the knees takes part of body weight, so the pull is lighter than a free pull-up (clinical opinion)
Pull-up and chin-up variations load the latissimus heavily; the chin-up adds biceps (Youdas 2010)
About 1.3 s up, short pause, about 2 s down (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #11597, Lever Assisted Chin-up, video (movement reference)
Youdas et al. 2010, surface EMG activation patterns and elbow joint motion during a pull-up, chin-up, or perfect-pullup rotational exercise (J Strength Cond Res 24(12):3404-3414)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
Step onto the knee pad one knee at a time while holding the handles; step off the same way.
More counterweight means more help: start with enough assistance to reach the top with control.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Shoulder discomfort at the bottom: stop just short of a full hang.
Elbow discomfort: use the neutral handles if the machine has them.

muscleNotes.lats_r: Prime mover: pulls the body up to the handles (Youdas 2010 for pull-up and chin-up muscle activity).
muscleNotes.lats_l: Prime mover: pulls the body up to the handles (Youdas 2010 for pull-up and chin-up muscle activity).
muscleNotes.biceps_r: Works harder with the underhand grip (Youdas 2010).
muscleNotes.biceps_l: Works harder with the underhand grip (Youdas 2010).
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_r: Draws the shoulder blades down and together.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_l: Draws the shoulder blades down and together.
muscleNotes.core: Keeps the body steady on the knee pad.
